question.problem: The axis of symmetry of the parabola $y=-(3x+4)(6x-k)$ is $x=-\frac{1}{3}.$ The value of $k=$
question.worked_solution:
First, we will calculate the axis of symmetry in terms of $k.$ Then, since we know that the axis of symmetry is $x=-\frac{1}{3},$ we will set our result equal to $-\frac{1}{3}.$ 

From the equation $y=-(3x+4)(6x-k),$ we find that the roots of the parabola are ${x}_{1}=-\frac{4}{3}$ and ${x}_{2}=\frac{k}{6}.$ 

To find the axis of symmetry, we take the average of the roots, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =\frac{{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}}{2} \\  & =\frac{(-\frac{4}{3}+\frac{k}{6})}{2} \\  & =\frac{(-\frac{8}{6}+\frac{k}{6})}{2} \\  & =\frac{k-8}{12}\end{aligned}
$$

We know that the axis of symmetry is $x=-\frac{1}{3}.$ Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{k-8}{12} & =-\frac{1}{3} \\ k-8 & =-4 \\ k & =-4+8 \\ k & =4.\end{aligned}
$$
